title: Atomic field-path register — Game Representation Specification revision 4
version: 2, after the stage A review (fidelity and determinism; the review did not look at slice items)

rowKinds.COLLECTION: The existence and count of elements in a collection. Items on a COLLECTION row say that elements matching a selector exist (EXISTS), how many (COUNT/RANGE), or that none may (NOT_EXISTS).
rowKinds.FIELD: An atomic property of one element, or of the game for non-collection rows.
rowKinds.VIEW: Computed from other rows, never stored. Items may constrain a view (checked in Gate B forward); a view never needs support and supports no stored row. Every contract still declares it.

fillableIsExhaustive: A free choice (REALIZATION) is possible only on rows with a 'fillable' entry, and only as that entry says (proposal P-4, applied for this run). sourceKinds is descriptive and licenses nothing.

rows.lateralValues: closed list (draft, AM-17), each with its interval test against the element's position.across, on an envelope of width W with the midline at W/2. wide-left: touches the 0 touchline and does not contain the midline. wide-right: touches the W touchline and does not contain the midline. wide: either of those. central: THE SAME TEST AS relativeTerms.central, which is canonical - contains the axis midline across the width, and touches neither touchline. full-width: touches both touchlines. An element matching none carries no lateral value. A lateral selector identifies an existing region; it never creates one (AM-13 preserved). These five values are a capability offered to CONTRACT AUTHORS: derivation never rewrites an authored selector or scope to use them (AM-12), so an existing contract gains nothing from AM-17 until it is restated

comparison.note: AM-16 as extended by Christian on 20 September and closed by his rulings the same day [C20b]. Requirement kind COMPARES. Classified under SD-29 as a bounded structural-semantic extension to the contribution/derivation grammar; the Game Representation data shape is unchanged and no ninth area is authorized.
comparison.operandForms: SD-23. Either (a) a represented game property: { row, selector }; or (b) a deterministically derived quantity whose inputs are SUPPORTED represented game properties: { derived: <named rule>, args }. Region value is NOT added as a stored row to support this. A derived quantity may compute relationships among represented environmental properties; it may not derive learner or ecological states (pressure, opportunity, affordance availability, difficulty, uncertainty)
comparison.inputsMustBeSupported: SD-23. A derived operand whose input the game states but nothing supports is not computable. Before SD-25 the primary event's base value rested only on engine wording, so no region's effective value was computable at all
comparison.relation: NARROWS. Never written with EXCLUSION strictness: a comparative is a relationship, not a prohibition [C20]. It never entails a value and never entails existence
comparison.whereItLands: SD-26. A comparison takes NO LINE. It is a relationship assertion evaluated over its operands, held in the contribution and reconciliation record, outside the eight stored areas. It never takes a property's verdict and never changes a line's status. This replaces the earlier reachesLine rule, which Christian overruled
comparison.boundary: Both operands must be properties the resolved game contains and can evaluate. Never an inferred player state or ecological outcome: not pressure, opportunity, affordance availability, difficulty or uncertainty
comparison.evaluability: SD-26. A comparison is evaluable only when both operands resolve - to a value the game holds and supports, or to a derived quantity whose inputs it holds and supports. Otherwise it is unmet (required) or not evaluable (supporting), by its requirement status. Never quietly true
comparison.relationshipConflict: SD-26. Two comparative requirements that no single assignment satisfies produce an UNRESOLVED RELATIONSHIP CONFLICT - a report of its own kind, not a line status and not a Game status. Raised only when both are authoritative (authored or owner-ruled, never assumed, never engine-only), both well-formed under SD-23, and both evaluable. Fail any of those and it is a gap, a diagnostic tension, or an unmet item instead
comparison.assumedCannotCollide: SD-27. An assumed item may not create an authoritative collision with authored knowledge. Assumed-vs-authored is reported diagnostically as a POSSIBLE TENSION, which no gate reads; it can never drive UNRESOLVED. An interpretation consistent with an object's prose is not promoted to canonical meaning
comparison.gapBeforeCollision: SD-28. A collision requires well-formed, support-capable authoritative claims with sufficiently resolved operands. An unauthored or incomputable dependency is a GAP first, and nothing downstream converts it into a disagreement. An invented or assumed comparative cannot manufacture an authoritative collision
comparison.effectiveValue: SD-24, provisional, in his words: the primary-event base value after application of all applicable resolved value modifiers for the referent. A value modifier must explicitly declare its operation or type (row V9a); multiplier versus increment is never inferred. If an operation or magnitude required for the derivation is unauthored, effective value is NOT COMPUTABLE
comparison.notAnExclusion: A comparative claim is not translated into a mutual exclusion. 'Wide has greater task value than central' is a relationship; it is not 'central value is forbidden' [C20]
comparison.stillOpen: No aggregate function is named (each, some, the sum, the greatest) for a comparison ranging over several matched elements. An engine refuses such a comparison rather than choosing one

relativeTerms.note: Interval tests for relative positions (RC-21). The referent must be a game element; if it is players or play, the item is OUTSIDE_BOUNDARY.
relativeTerms.beyond X (for team T): the element's near edge is at or past X's far edge, in T's attacking direction
relativeTerms.own end (of team T): touches the end line T defends
relativeTerms.attacking end (of team T): touches the end line T attacks
relativeTerms.central: contains the axis midline across the width, and touches neither touchline
relativeTerms.lengthwise: the element's extent along the axis is at least its extent across it (AM-22; renamed from 'longitudinal' to avoid colliding with the lateral selector attribute)

citableStandingDecisions.restricts: No reconciliation or rendering step may remove an objective element from J1, or change its J4 role away from REPRESENTATIVE, on the ground that it is not the primary scoring objective
citableStandingDecisions.note: Retyped 20 September. It was typed as an EXISTS/EQUALS item whose value was the prose phrase functionally necessary to the representative game structure, which no requirement kind can express - so as typed it could never fire and supported nothing. His decision is a prohibition on removal, not a source of support, so it is typed as one. OPEN, and his: the machine test for functionally necessary. The candidate is that a support-capable item of some selected object references the objective (J2, or a selector that matches it), but that is a reading, not his words. Until he fixes the test, SD-10 restricts removal only where such a reference exists
